corrections.claimed_speedup: SPLITJOIN: buffet 1397 ns vs C++ 3317 ns vs C 2782 ns (~2.4x vs the C++ version, derived from page data). But SPLITJOIN_cpp in src/bench.cpp splits into vector<std::string_view> and joins into a malloc'd char*, so it does not use std::string. Against real std::string (APPEND_cpp), buffet is 30.2 vs 36.5 ns at 8/16, 30.1 vs 49.0 ns at 24/4 and 28.8 vs 48.1 ns at 24/32 (~1.2-1.7x, derived from page data), but slower at 8/4 (16.3 vs 10.9 ns). MEMVIEW: std::string_view 0.609 ns vs buffet 6.36 ns, so buffet is slower. MEMCOPY compares only against C, not std::string.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: g++ -std=c++2a -fpermissive -g -O2 for src/bench.cpp; libbuffet built with gcc -std=c11 -O2 -DNDEBUG (per repo Makefile); harness is Google Benchmark
corrections.caveats: Author explicitly states "the lib is not much optimized and the bench maybe amateurish"; CPU model not stated ("weak Core i3"); only libstdc++ (via g++) exercised; the headline SPLITJOIN 'C++' baseline is a hand-written std::string_view split + malloc join, not std::string; against std::string proper (APPEND) the win is ~1.2-1.7x at some sizes and a loss at 8/4; std::string_view wins MEMVIEW by ~10x.

notes: The numbers match the README exactly. The 'faster than std::string' framing for split/join is a mislabel, because that benchmark uses std::string_view. The legitimate std::string win is the APPEND benchmark (up to ~1.7x). The default branch is main, and the old master raw URL still redirects.
